name: Topaz Video Upscale
description: Upscale videos with Topaz Labs enhancement models, optionally raising the frame rate in the same job. One endpoint; the `model` request field picks the enhancement model (Proteus by default). Starlight models are priced per output frame, at a higher rate when the output's long edge exceeds 1920px. Proteus is priced per output megapixel.

upscale_factor.description: Output scale. `x1` means no upscale: the job carries only the frame-interpolation filter and the output keeps the source resolution, so it requires `target_fps` and forbids the proteus tuning controls (they belong to the upscale filter that `x1` omits). `x1` is a widening of the enum — the default is still `x2`.
upscale_factor.title: Upscale Factor

model.description: Topaz enhancement model. `proteus` (default) is the general-purpose upscaler; the `starlight-*` models are the slower, higher-quality diffusion family (sources up to 30fps, output up to 4K). Except `starlight-precise-2.6`, which scales exactly by upscale_factor, starlight output never drops below 720p — small sources come back larger than upscale_factor alone implies.
model.title: Model

recover_detail.description: How much original detail to preserve (proteus only).
recover_detail.title: Recover Detail

h264_output.description: Encode the output with H.264 instead of the default H.265.
h264_output.title: H264 Output

target_fps.description: Raise the output frame rate to this value (15-240, decimals allowed for the NTSC rates 23.976/29.97/59.94) with Topaz's Apollo frame-interpolation model, in the same job as the upscale (proteus only). The output duration is unchanged — only the frame rate goes up — and the target must exceed the source's own frame rate. Omitted keeps the source frame rate.
target_fps.title: Target Fps
